statement: Across all 60 model-horizon-scope comparisons, F4 has lower point-estimate MAE than F3 in 35 cases and higher MAE in 25 cases.
The paired calendar-day block-bootstrap 95% CI lies entirely above zero in 12 comparisons, entirely below zero in 16 comparisons, and crosses zero in 32 comparisons.
The F3 -> F4 effect is not universal: both favorable and unfavorable resolved effects occur across the frozen model families.
The 30-minute horizon contains more resolved positive than resolved negative F3 -> F4 comparisons in both all-row and daylight evaluation.
At 60 minutes, resolved negative F3 -> F4 effects are more common than resolved positive effects in both evaluation scopes.
Ridge and GRU show consistently negative F3 -> F4 effects across all six evaluated horizon-scope combinations, with every 95% CI below zero.
TCN exhibits a resolved horizon reversal: F4 reduces MAE relative to F3 at 15 and 30 minutes in both scopes, but increases MAE at 60 minutes in both scopes.
For HGBR and XGBoost, all six point estimates favor F4, but every corresponding 95% CI crosses zero.
F3 -> F4 improvement must be interpreted as incremental information beyond the continuous astronomical representation, not as proof that F4 is the globally best feature family.
The Phase-1 experiment supports predictive and representational conclusions only and does not establish a physical causal influence of Panchang categories on photovoltaic generation.
